newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Some 6,000 Zairean refugees head for Zambia - UNHCR.
newsitem.headline: Some 6,000 Zairean refugees head for Zambia - UNHCR.

text.p: At least 6,000 people fleeing Zaire's civil war were expected to arrive in neighbouring Zambia in barges later on Thursday, the United Nations refugee agency (UNHCR) said.
"We are expecting some 6,000 Zairean refugees in the country within the next few hours," UNHCR protection officer Ron Mponda told Reuters.
The refugees were travelling in barges to Zambia's northern Mpulungu district across Lake Tanganyika, he said.
This would bring to around 8,300 the number of Zaireans who have crossed the border into Zambia since October 1996 when rebels started their campaign in east Zaire.
Mponda said soldiers were among those fleeing Zaire.
"Eight soldiers laid down their arms and will be granted refugee status along with the rest," he said.
"The authorities -- police, the army and immigration -- have been posted to the border area to ensure that there is proper screening of the new arrivals," he said.
Mponda said 1,000 refugees were already accommodated at the Maheba refugee camp in northwestern Solwezi district.
Some 300 refugees waiting to be transferred to the camp were housed in a hall in Mpulungu, while the rest were still on the barges that brought them to Zambia.
Mponda said the refugees faced water shortages and plans were underway to ferry water to them.
